title: "About"
subtitle: "Data sources, limitations, and how to contribute"

## What this is

A reproducible R pipeline that nowcasts Australian quarterly Net
Overseas Migration (NOM) from public data only, and republishes the
result as a static website on a weekly cadence. The site you're
reading is regenerated from scratch by a GitHub Actions workflow that
fetches the latest ABS / DHA data, refits the model, and pushes the
rendered HTML to GitHub Pages.

The codebase is on GitHub: [DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast](https://github.com/DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast).
Pull requests welcome.

## Data sources

| Source | What | Update cadence | Publication lag |
|--------|------|----------------|-----------------|
| ABS Overseas Arrivals and Departures (cat. 3401.0) | Long-term arrivals / departures by visa group | Monthly | ~5 weeks |
| ABS Quarterly Population Estimates (cat. 3101.0) | Headline NOM total | Quarterly | ~6 months |
| Department of Home Affairs (via data.gov.au CKAN) | Visa grants by program (Student, Skilled, Working Holiday, Temporary Graduate; Visitor is fetched but excluded from the model) | Financial-year pivots, re-issued quarterly | ~45 days |

The ABS annual NOM-by-visa cube (cat. 3407.0) has a fetcher but is
switched off until the per-category estimator consumes it.

All sources are accessible via free public APIs / file downloads.
Fetchers live in [`R/ingest/`](https://github.com/DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast/tree/main/R/ingest).

## Limitations

- **No private microdata.** Without PLIDA-level stay-duration data the
  model can't directly observe the 12/16-month rule. It estimates the
  OAD-to-NOM mapping empirically from completed cohorts.
- **No granular quarterly visa breakdown.** ABS retired quarterly
  NOM-by-visa publication. The model uses annual FY visa data
  broadcast across quarters via OAD-arrival proportions.
- **Mixed-mode backtest.** ABS NOM vintages have been captured weekly
  since May 2026, so backtest origins from then on are genuinely
  vintage-aware; earlier origins are pseudo-real-time (today's values,
  restricted to what was publicly observable then). The vintage-aware
  share grows one quarter per ABS release.
- **Single-series headline.** The Bayesian headline models total NOM
  only; the per-category decomposition still comes from the Phase 1
  univariate Kalman filters and an empirical classification ratio.

## How the site is built

```
Weekly (Mondays)
  │
  ├── 05:30 UTC  Refresh headline (Bayes)   → data/headline_bayes.rds
  │                cmdstanr + bayes_kalman HMC fit, ~75 s, committed to main
  ├── 06:00 UTC  Render and deploy          (also on every push to main)
  │     ├── Install R 4.4 + Quarto (RSPM binaries, cached)
  │     ├── targets::tar_make()
  │     │     ├── Fetch ABS OAD via {readabs}
  │     │     ├── Fetch ABS NOM (cat. 3101.0)
  │     │     ├── Fetch DHA visa grants via data.gov.au CKAN
  │     │     ├── Build quarterly panel (partial-quarter handling)
  │     │     ├── Estimate pi (empirical + smoothed)
  │     │     ├── Fit univariate Kalman per category (Phase 1)
  │     │     ├── Fit multivariate Kalman with Gamma lag (Phase 2 v4.0)
  │     │     └── Run benchmarks (bridge, RW, AR1)
  │     ├── Verify core inputs arrived
  │     ├── quarto render  (this site)
  │     └── actions/deploy-pages → GitHub Pages
  └── 22:00 UTC  Capture NOM vintage        → data/vintages/nom_history.csv

Monthly (1st): Refresh backtest (all models incl. Bayes) → data/backtest_scored.rds
On push / PR:  Tests (testthat)
```

End-to-end render time: ~10 minutes with a warm package cache.

## Model architecture in one paragraph

A Bayesian state-space model (`bayes_kalman`) with three observation
rows — OAD long-term arrivals, visa grants with a discretised Gamma
lag, and quarterly NOM itself — all loading on a single latent
log-arrivals state with a damped local-linear trend. The latent state
is integrated out by a Kalman filter inside Stan, so HMC samples only
the ~10 static parameters and the credible intervals are proper
posterior intervals. The headline NOM forecast comes directly from the
latent state via a calibrated offset, bypassing the empirical-π
extrapolation that earlier model versions relied on. Full equations
on the [Methodology](methodology.qmd) page.

## Contributing

The codebase uses standard R/`{targets}`/Quarto idioms. Open issues
and PRs are welcome:

- [Open issues](https://github.com/DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast/issues)
- [Open pull request](https://github.com/DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast/pulls)
- [STATUS.md](https://github.com/DavidAStephan/NOM_Nowcast/blob/main/STATUS.md) lists the current model version, recent
  backtest numbers, and the open punch-list.

Areas that could use help:

- **Per-category modelling.** The Bayesian headline is aggregate only.
  Per-visa-category fits with cross-category partial pooling would
  give a category decomposition of the headline; the hierarchical Stan
  scaffold exists but is uncalibrated.
- **Better leading indicators.** The DHA temporary-visa-holder stock
  (BP0019 on data.gov.au) and BITRE airline passenger data are obvious
  candidates; the current fetchers target pages that moved to Power BI
  and are switched off.
- **Monthly visa grants.** The CKAN pivots are financial-year totals
  spread across quarters by OAD shares; a monthly or quarterly grant
  series would sharpen the leading signal considerably.
